seo.metaTitle: Swap PNG Orientation - Force Portrait or Landscape
seo.metaDescription: Make an image portrait or landscape the way you ask: it turns by 90 degrees only when the orientation does not match. Free, no upload, no signup, lossless.
seo.longDescription: Swapping the orientation sets an image to the orientation you want by turning it a quarter turn when it does not already match. Pick Portrait and a landscape picture is rotated by 90 degrees clockwise into portrait; pick Landscape and a portrait one is turned the other way. If the image already has the orientation you asked for, it is returned untouched, and the same goes for a square image, which has no orientation to swap and comes back pixel-identical. Because the turn is a right angle, the pixels are only moved to new positions: no resampling, no interpolation and no quality loss at all. Use it when a batch of photos has to match one orientation for a gallery, a print sheet or a device screen. Everything runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Check the preview: it turns only if the current orientation differs from your choice.
Download the result from the Download button.

faq.q: What happens to a square image?
faq.a: Nothing: a square is neither portrait nor landscape, so there is no orientation to swap and the tool returns it unchanged. Set a target size in the change canvas size tool if you need it inside a square frame.

faq.q: Is it the same as rotating by 90 degrees?
faq.a: Almost. Rotating by 90 always turns the image, while swapping only turns it when the result differs from the orientation you chose, so an already-correct file passes through untouched.

No. The turn is by 90 degrees, so whole pixels are relocated to new positions with no interpolation and no re-compression inside the tool. For any other angle use the rotate free tool, which resamples and softens edges slightly.

It turns 90 degrees clockwise when the orientation has to change, the same direction as the 90 degree option in the rotate tool. For a counter-clockwise quarter turn, run the rotate tool and pick 270 degrees.
